note: 'Abishai, the brother of Joab, was chief of the Three ... even though he was not included among the Three' (1Chr 11:20-21).
'These were the exploits of Benaiah son of Jehoiada, who won a name alongside the three mighty men ... And David appointed him over his guard' (1Chr 11:24-25).

'Now David had said, “Whoever is the first to strike down a Jebusite will become chief commander.” And Joab son of Zeruiah went up first, and he became the chief.' (1Chr 11:6). **The command is the appointment**: the post is offered as a prize before anyone has won it.

'He built up the city around it, from the supporting terraces to the surrounding wall' (1Chr 11:8). The verse says 'he'; David is named at 11:7, 'So David took up residence in the fortress; that is why it was called the City of David'.
'where David made a covenant with them before the LORD' (1Chr 11:3).
'Now these were the chiefs of David's mighty men, who, together with all Israel, bolstered and strengthened his kingdom' (1Chr 11:10).
'And they anointed him king over Israel, according to the word of the LORD through Samuel.' (1Chr 11:3) -- the chronicler tying the act back to 1 Samuel 16.
Made with 'all the elders of Israel', who had come to Hebron saying 'Here we are, your own flesh and blood' (1Chr 11:1).

'Jashobeam son of Hachmoni was chief of the officers; he wielded his spear against three hundred men, whom he killed at one time.' (1Chr 11:11).; Entailed rather than stated: the text identifies the person by tribe, or names a parent of that tribe.
'He built up the city around it, from the supporting terraces to the surrounding wall, while Joab restored the rest of the city.' (1Chr 11:8).
